chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever catches the 'Jam' (concurrent Hajj and 'Umrah), has caught the Hajj.

And Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whichever pilgrim, bringing his offering (Hady) or performing individual Hajj or performing 'Umrah with conjunction to Hajj, arrives and his Hajj has been missed, let him make it an 'Umrah, and upon him is the Hajj next year.

key_terms.جَمْعًا: Concurrent Hajj and 'Umrah (Hajj al-Tamattu' or Hajj al-Qiran)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ بِالْعُمْرَةِ: One performing 'Umrah with conjunction to Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the Hajj season while performing their rituals?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) regarding the status of pilgrims who arrive after the Hajj season has concluded. The Imam clarifies that whether one is a Qarin (combining Hajj and Umrah), Mufrid (Hajj only), or Mutamatti’ (Umrah then Hajj), missing the Hajj time converts the current sacrifice into an Umrah, while the Hajj obligation remains deferred to the next year. This highlights the Shia juristic view on the flexibility of ritual conversion and the persistence of the primary duty despite temporal delays.
